passage:
Vaibhav's father had taken a loan from the co-operative society to send him to the engineering college in the district town. Every time Vaibhav came home on the local bus, the loan sat between them at dinner like an extra plate.

This semester he failed a paper. For two weeks he told his mother, Indu, on the phone that everything was fine. She heard the flatness in his voice anyway.

On Sunday he sat beside her on the verandah while she picked stones from the rice. "Ma, I failed one paper. I didn't say because I'm ashamed."

Indu kept picking stones. "I knew something was wrong. Tell me how we fix it."

He said he'd retake it and start Saturday tutoring for the neighbourhood children. She nodded. "Study first. The money is my worry, not something for you to hide behind."

His shame loosened. The loan did not shrink.

qa.q: Why did Vaibhav hide the failure for two weeks?
qa.a: He was ashamed and did not want to disappoint his parents, who had taken a loan for his education.

qa.q: What plan does Vaibhav make to deal with the failed paper?
qa.a: He will retake it and start Saturday tutoring for the neighbourhood children, keeping study first.

qa.q: How did Indu see Vaibhav's silence?
qa.a: She had already heard the flatness in his voice and sensed something was wrong, so she was more worried about him than about the paper.

grounding: Family sacrifice for Vaibhav's education weighs on him; he hides a failure, then is honest and plans to study seriously and work a little.

passage:
Result day, and Ramesh's phone showed two missed calls from Amma and 8 per cent battery. On the screen at the cyber café in Warangal: Mathematics III, FAIL.
His parents had pledged Amma's gold to pay his fees. He had seen her bare wrists for two years.
His first thought was to say "all cleared" and quietly retake it in the summer. No one would know.
Gurleen, at the next computer, saw his face. "Backlog?"
"One. They pledged the gold for me, Gurleen."
"Then they deserve the truth more than anyone. And one backlog can be fixed."
His phone died before he could decide. He borrowed the café's landline and called home anyway. "Amma, I failed Maths III. I'm going to clear it in the supplementary exam. I'll join the free tutoring on campus and take evening shifts at the print shop to pay the exam fee myself."
Amma was quiet. Then: "Thank you for telling us. Eat something before you come home."

qa.q: Why did Ramesh think of saying "all cleared"?
qa.a: He felt ashamed and guilty about Amma's pledged gold and afraid of disappointing his parents.

qa.q: What did Ramesh do instead of hiding it?
qa.a: He told Amma the truth on the café landline along with a plan: the supplementary exam, free campus tutoring and evening print-shop shifts for the fee.
Quietly at first, then with thanks for telling them and care ("Eat something"), valuing his honesty.

grounding: Shows the weight of family sacrifice for education, the pull to hide a failure, and choosing honesty with a plan to study and work part time.

passage:
Hansa's Baba had taken a loan from the cooperative bank to send her to design college in Kolkata, and every Sunday on the phone she said, "Everything's great, Baba."
It wasn't. Her rent had gone up, she was skipping lunches, and she had been too tired to finish two assignments.
Her cousin Kishore, who worked at a bank branch in Salt Lake, noticed at his birthday dinner. "You look exhausted. Tell me the truth."
She did, for the first time. Then: "I can't tell Baba. He'll think the loan was a mistake."
"He'll think that if you fail because you hid it," Kishore said. "Tell him what's hard and what you're doing about it."
That Sunday she did. "Baba, the rent went up. I'm taking a weekend job at the print studio near college, it's related to my course, and I've spoken to my professor about the two late assignments."
Baba was quiet. Then: "You should have told me earlier. But good. Study first. The job only on weekends."

qa.a: At a bank branch in Salt Lake.

qa.q: Why had Hansa kept saying "Everything's great"?
qa.a: She felt guilty about the loan and afraid Baba would think it had been a mistake.

qa.q: What made Hansa's call to Baba an honest update?
qa.a: She said what was hard (rent, skipped lunches, two late assignments) and what she was doing: a weekend print-studio job and talking to her professor.

qa.q: How does Baba take Hansa's news?
qa.a: He wishes she had told him earlier, but approves, as long as study comes first and the job stays on weekends.

grounding: Illustrates a family loan weighing on a student, hiding struggles to avoid disappointing them, and then being honest and working part time.
